mechanism_narrative: A positive 3-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as stronger manufacturing output directly correlates with near-term corporate earnings growth without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where INDPRO has increased by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS has been above 5.0% for at least 3 months, or the Rank IC remains above 0.03 in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates housing sector weakness amid labor market tightness, creating economic uncertainty that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where HOUST has decreased by at least 1% and UNRATE has decreased by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 jobs signals accelerating economic recovery, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 jobs, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation requiring aggressive central bank intervention, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC remains above 0.03 in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Positive year-over-year growth in real GDP (GDPC1) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as sustained economic expansion supports corporate earnings growth without regime-specific conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where GDPC1 growth is positive year-over-year, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals contractionary monetary policy coinciding with manufacturing weakness, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS has increased by at least 0.25% and INDPRO has decreased by at least 0.5% over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During low housing demand regimes (HOUST < 1900 thousand units), a monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of at least 5% signals sector recovery, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where HOUST is below 1900 and increases by at least 5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
